To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Q factor of a laser can be passively switched by bleaching molecular vapor, and the resulting pulses are shorter and more energetic than those from other passive Q switches.
we have demonstrated a novel passive Q switch based on the photodissociative bleaching of molecular iodine vapor that is capable of producing 0.7 J pulses
we have shown that a ruby laser can be passively Q switched by a molecular gas, in this case iodine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the production of short pulses of high energy.
the development of the technology for the production of high-power, short-pulse, tunable radiation in the visible and ultraviolet spectral regions.
the use of molecular iodine vapor for the passive Q switching of solid‐state lasers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown a new method of passive Q switching of a laser by means of molecular iodine vapor, which is a simple, effective, and reliable method.
the iodine Q switch is a very effective device for producing high-energy pulses of short duration, which can be easily and inexpensively produced in large quantities.
the authors of this paper have made a very significant contribution to the field of Q switching and the use of molecular iodine vapor for Q switching is a very important and useful development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iodine vapor Q switch is a simple, reliable, and efficient device for the generation of high-energy picosecond laser pulses in a wide range of wavelengths.
the iodine vapor is a very efficient passive Q switch for the ruby laser.

the iodine vapor Q switch has the following advantages over other known passive Q switches: 1) the iodine vapor Q switching is reversible; 2) the energy of the laser pulses is not reduced during the Q switching; 3) it is possible to obtain a large number of pulses with a repetition rate of 10 ^{3}  Hz; 4) the Q switch is not destroyed during its operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular iodine vapor is a promising candidate for the passive Q switching of solid state lasers.
the use of molecular iodine vapor for Q switching of ruby lasers is promising.
the Q-switching effect is due to photodissociative absorption of iodine molecules in the visible range.
